findings.reason: this is §5's only measure of the new questions' routing quality, so a worker can ship an incorrect lane-and-model questions template and still pass the section's headline check; the done-when needs an assertion that can fail (for example a negative control that widens `offered` to include a refused pair and shows the questions/refusal path reject it), otherwise the section closes on a property the harness enforces regardless of the change.
findings.text: §5's first done-when, "a replay of at least 50 recorded dispatches through the new questions sends 0 picks to a refused or logged-out model", cannot fail: `snapshot.candidates` appends a reason for availability in {refused, unavailable, logged-out} (reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:565) so those candidates are removed from `offered` before Jev sees them (picker/__init__.py:84), and `pick()` resolves the choice only by `next(c for c in offered if c.backend == choice)` (picker/__init__.py:128), so a non-offered backend raises and falls back rather than being picked; `replay._summary.picked_refused` therefore always reads 0 (reckon/crew/picker/replay.py:109-145).
